Title: Trump threatens to revoke citizenship of naturalized immigrants convicted of fraud - as it happened
Date: 2026-01-14

Content: At issue is whether these state bans violate the US constitution’s 14th amendment, which ensures the law applies equally to all, or Title IX, which prohibits sex discrimination. Earlier, justice Neil Gorsuch chimed in with a big question about whether transgender people should be considered a legally protected class. Gorsuch, a member of the court’s conservative majority, is one of the most closely watched justices in this case. He wrote a key 2020 decision upholding workplace discrimination protections for transgender people, but in 2025 joined the majority in allowing states to ban certain healthcare for transgender youth. Alan Hurst, Idaho’s solicitor general arguing in defense of the state’s ban, replied saying that he did not question there has been “some discrimination against transgender people, significant discrimination” in the US, but said it did not compare with that historically faced by Black people and women.

Title: Supreme court appears sympathetic towards state bans for transgender athletes in school sports – as it happened
Date: 2026-01-13

Content: Gorsuch, a member of the court’s conservative majority, is one of the most closely watched justices in this case. He wrote a key 2020 decision upholding workplace discrimination protections for transgender people, but in 2025 joined the majority in allowing states to ban certain healthcare for transgender youth. Hurst replied that he did not question there has been “some discrimination against transgender people, significant discrimination” in the United States, but said it did not compare with that historically faced by black people and women. On the issue of whether the case is moot, the justices have said they would wait to make a decision about whether to dismiss it until after today’s argument. A reminder that Lindsay Hecox, the transgender college student who challenged Idaho’s state law, sought to have her case dismissed in September, arguing that she is no longer pursuing sports and doesn’t want further harassment.

initial_question.answer: As of January 13, 2026, the justices were waiting to decide whether to dismiss the case because Lindsay Hecox had sought to have it dismissed in September, arguing she was no longer pursuing sports and wanted to avoid further harassment; this legal backdrop coincides with Alan Hurst's subsequent argument on January 14, 2026, where he conceded that significant discrimination against transgender people exists in the U.S. while simultaneously defending the state's ban by claiming it does not reach the same historical level of discrimination as that faced by Black people and women.
